newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 4.00-5.00 cents higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 4.00-5.00 cents higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 4.00 to 5.00 cents higher Wednesday in a technical correction to Tuesday's massive sell-off, traders said.
But some traders said the market was more likely to come in unchanged to lower, as they expected to see follow-through to the downside.
"There's some commission house sell orders," said one floor trader. "And the ring is long, so that will put some pressure on it early. They are looking to take it below $2 (basis July)."

Tuesday, New York arabica futures plummeted to one-month lows on speculative selling amid forecasts for mild weather in top-grower Brazil. Spot July ended down 35.35 cents at 217.95 cents after trading from 256.00 to 235.50. September dropped 26.85 to 196.75, while the back months fell 12.40 to 19.30.
The July/September spread pulled in sharply Tuesday, ending at 21.20 cents compared with 29.70 cents on Monday.
On the weather front, no damaging cold weather is expected in Brazil's coffee regions through early next week, Weather Services Corp. said in its daily report on Wednesday.
In other news, Association of Indonesian Coffee Exporters' chairman Oesman Soedargo said he expected Indonesia's coffee production to drop 160,000 tonnes to 290,000 tonnes in 1997.
Soedargo also predicted the 1997 exportable amount to fall to 180,000 tonnes from 330,000 tonnes this year.
After Tuesday's close, the CSCE said certified coffee stocks fell by 213 60-kg bags as of June 9, to 44,002 bags, however, there were 7,000 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
London robusta futures were sharply lower early Wednesday, pounded by speculative liquidation. LIFFE July fell $122 at the midday break, to $1,698, while September lost $128, to $1,722.
